list.Title: R--Purdue Advanced Reactor Core Simulator Code
list.Description: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing a presolicitation notice for a requirement entitled, Technical Support for the Purdue Advanced Reactor Core Simulator (PARCS) Code Suite The objective of this acquisition is to obtain regulatory technical support for the maintenance, code support, assessment, continued development, and user training of the PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS code suite, including the interfaces between PARCS and RELAP, TRACE, and SNAP. These activities ensure that the PARCS code suite remains a reliable and modern tool for confirmatory reactor physics and systems analysis. PARCS supports independent regulatory decision making by enabling NRC staff to perform confirmatory evaluations of operator actions, core designs, power uprates, advanced reactor concepts, and license amendment requests. Maintaining and advancing the PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS capability is essential for enabling high quality staff reviews under 10 CFR Parts 50 and 52. At a high level, this acquisition will:  Maintain and support the PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS code suite, including version control, regression testing, documentation upkeep, bug identification, and corrective maintenance.  Develop and evaluate new code functionality, models, numerical methods, and interfaces needed to support emerging regulatory needs, advanced reactor designs, and new cross section methodologies.  Provide confirmatory analysis support, including model development, coupled system assessments, technical consultation, and code user guidance for NRC staff and program offices.  Deliver training and knowledge transfer activities to ensure NRC staff and authorized users can effectively apply PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS for regulatory analyses. The period of performance is five years with a 1-year base period and four 1-year optional periods. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the services required is 541990 All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services. Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 31310027R0003 will be posted on, or about, December 2, 2026, as full and open competition under FAR Part 15. list.Description: In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 5.201 and 5.203, the U.S. Army Contracting Command - Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Orlando Division, on behalf of the U.S. Army Security Assistance Training Management Organization (USASATMO), intends to issue a competitive Request for Proposals (RFP) for the Aviation Training Support Services (ATSS) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC). Services are divided into two primary functional categories: (1) Training-Related Services and (2) Technical Assistance-Related Services. Required capabilities include tactical flight instruction, maintenance test flight operations, aircraft servicing, maintenance, armament, and operational planning on both Standard U.S. Military Aircraft (e.g., AH-64D/E Apache) and Non-Standard Rotary-Wing and Fixed-Wing Aircraft (e.g., Mi-17, Bell 407/412, Cessna 208).
